framework: Japan AISI - Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety v1.10 (28 Mar 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Defines ten evaluation perspectives: toxic output control; misinformation and manipulation; fairness and inclusion; high-risk/unintended use; privacy; security; explainability; robustness; data quality; verifiability.
what_is_tested: Ten safety perspectives for LLM systems
who_tests: Development and provision managers; experts inside or outside the organisation; third-party evaluation can complement (Sec. 4.1)

requirement_paraphrase: Recommends AI-specific penetration testing of AI system components before deployment and periodically afterwards, including testing outputs and system behaviour.
what_is_tested: Exploitable cybersecurity weaknesses in AI components and behaviour

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Principle 2, Deploy and Monitor item 3, p. 17
requirement_paraphrase: The AI system should be tested to ensure the combination of available data does not reveal sensitive data or break anonymity.

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
clause_or_page: Objectives, point A; EC Code page
requirement_paraphrase: The Code is a voluntary tool for demonstrating compliance with Arts. 53 and 55 and states that adherence is not conclusive evidence of compliance; the Commission and AI Board have confirmed it as an adequate voluntary tool.
what_is_tested: Compliance demonstration route for GPAI providers

requirement_paraphrase: The AI trustworthiness framework series is at mixed stages: Part 1 logging at stage 50, Part 3 human oversight at stage 40, Parts 2 (transparency), 4 (accuracy) and 5 (robustness) at stage 20; all flagged harmonised, none OJEU-referenced.

framework: US NIST AI 800-2 ipd (CAISI) Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models (Initial Public Draft, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Report qualified claims: distinguish observations, inferences, predictions and normative statements and tie claims to the evaluated benchmark and measurement conditions.
what_is_tested: Calibration of claims from test results

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Commission must issue standardisation requests covering all Section 2 requirements and request deliverables facilitating joint compliance with Chapter III Sections 2-3 and Annex I product legislation.
what_is_tested: Standardisation request (a duty on the Commission)
who_tests: European Commission (requesting); European standardisation organisations (CEN, CENELEC, ETSI)

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must notify the Commission within two weeks of meeting (or learning they will meet) the systemic-risk criterion, and may argue exceptionally that their model does not present systemic risks.

framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: The v2.0 decision takes effect on 1 Sep 2026; CAIO measures under Sec. 6.2 were to be set by 30 Jun 2026 and the AI governance framework scope under Sec. 2.2.2 applies from 1 Jul 2026.

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Toolkit (Digital Dubai consultation page)
requirement_paraphrase: Digital Dubai states the Executive Council advised that the toolkit is to be used by all public entities looking to implement AI systems.
what_is_tested: AI systems of public entities, via the self-assessment toolkit

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Content red teaming probes the app dynamically for blind spots, multi-turn failures and subjective harms; define targeted vs open-ended objectives; use domain experts, AI experts and target end users with diversity; track acceptable response rate, refusal rate and turns-to-unsafe; annotators may be red teamers, independent third parties or LLM judges with human sampling; automated red teaming (e.g. PAIR, Crescendo-style) is an emerging complement.
who_tests: Developers/deployers, domain experts, independent annotators, automated tools
